input.quote: 22.14 Solicitation. Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party during the Term of this Agreement, for any reason.
input.rationale: Section 22.14 binds Customer not to solicit any M&I employee, for any reason, for the entire Term, which the definitions fix at eight years from the Commencement Date (p0049). That fails the fallback on three material terms: it is not limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, it far exceeds 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, and there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. A restriction longer than 24 months covering all Vendor personnel is walk-away territory under this rule. It does at least stop short of a no-hire (it bars solicitation only). We therefore move to the preferred position with the shortest possible edit: Section 22.14 becomes one-way, so M&I remains restricted from soliciting our employees while no non-solicitation restriction binds Customer.

proposal.summary: Make Section 22.14 solicitation restriction one-way, binding only M&I
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that no non-solicitation restriction should bind us, so we have made Section 22.14 one-way: M&I remains restricted from soliciting our employees, and the restriction on Customer is removed. If M&I needs mutuality, we can accept a mutual clause limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party during the Term of this Agreement, for any reason.
ops.newText: M&I shall not solicit the employees of Customer during the Term of this Agreement, for any reason.
